source.title: What Makes a Representational Prior Work? Feature Families, Label-Free Invariances, and Critical Windows in Grokking

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Tests grokking outcomes and generalization timing under new representational-prior, timing-window, architecture, task, and norm-clamp conditions; it does not reproduce the original measurement setup in full.
record.gate_note: Rows record reported grokking fractions and generalization timing. The paper does not report training-accuracy trajectories or a training-set-size sweep, so it does not establish the full chance-to-near-perfect trajectory or that smaller training sets increase the delay. Some comparison arms are reused from the companion work, as stated in the paper. The synthetic-grammar findings are recorded under fits_no_version because they show immediate generalization followed by degradation, not a delayed-generalization result on the data types named by V3.
record.test_reason: Most rows measure the study's own contrastive-prior interventions against same-seed baselines; these are method-performance results, not tests of the claim. The study's own baseline runs do bear on the claim. They show delayed generalization on modular arithmetic (tgen about 20k epochs) and no delay on small sparse parity. A clamped-norm sweep with plain cross-entropy shows delay rising steeply with weight norm, which bears on the norm parts of V3 and V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors build on a companion claim that the grokking delay is the time to form task-structured representations. They conclude that feature-family alignment decides whether a prior permits generalization, that label-free invariance suffices for acceleration, and that a brief early window captures most of the benefit. Speed at the optimal norm belongs to norm control alone, while the prior flattens the norm-delay exponent ~17×. The account is limited to memorize-first tasks.
record.recipe_differences: This paper uses a one-layer transformer, a 30% split of modular addition, full-batch AdamW with weight decay 1.0, and adds supervised-contrastive priors, windowing, and norm clamps; details of the original recipe are not specified here.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with prior feature family, supervision, application window, task, architecture and normalization, and clamped weight norm. The paper reports slower or failed generalization for band/random priors, some unmitigated-prior architecture conditions, and the prior at very low norm.

fits_no_version.finding: On two synthetic subject–verb agreement grammars and on small parity, generalization is immediate and then degrades (grammar peak 0.90 by epoch 500, final 0.73). A prior raises levels but not the trend.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tasks where the rule is easier than memorization show no grokking delay and may degrade with continued training.

fits_no_version.finding: Contrastive representational priors aligned with the task's feature family accelerate grokking, while foreign-family or random priors block it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Injecting task-aligned representational structure controls whether and when grokking occurs.

record.problems: Sample sizes are 3–15 per cell, with 3 seeds for per-clamp-value cells; the CE exponent is a lower bound because high-norm cells are censored. The paper states that window boundaries were chosen a priori and not swept finely, early-window advantage is a median tendency with seed-level exceptions, and all runs use a single prime and training fraction. Training-accuracy trajectories and a training-set-size sweep are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: None of the separately stated numerical or explicit grokking outcomes relevant to the tested versions were omitted.

untested.parts: Training-accuracy saturation and the chance-level test-accuracy trajectory are not reported; there is no training-set-size sweep (single 30% split, single prime).
Not tested: no circuit analysis and no progress measures.
Non-algorithmic data (images, realistic text, molecules), initialization scale, and the lazy-to-rich transition are not tested.
Circuit efficiency, critical dataset size and ungrokking are not tested; weight decay itself is not varied (fixed at 1.0).
Not tested; full-batch AdamW is fixed throughout.

missing.what: Baseline (no prior) on (a+b) mod 97 groks 10/10 in the window experiment; this is the primary V1 baseline and has no row.
Shared low-norm floor below ~40–45 for both regimes; below it, delay no longer falls with norm.

record.verdict_notes: Most of the record's V1 rows measure the study's own interventions and were relinked to none. The verdicts rest on baseline arms and the plain-CE norm sweep. Training accuracy is never shown, so 'beyond overfitting' is assumed from the memorize-first framing. Small cells (3–15 seeds); single prime and split. The V5 support covers only the low-norm bias part, not the efficiency or critical-dataset predictions.

versions.untested_parts: No training-accuracy saturation or chance-level test-accuracy trajectory is reported; no training-set-size sweep tests whether delay grows as the training set shrinks.
The paper does not measure gradual formation of a generalizing circuit, later removal of memorizing components, or continuous progress measures anticipating a jump.
No grokking-like delayed generalization is tested on images, realistic text, or molecules; initialization-scale and lazy-to-rich transitions are not tested.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.

The paper tests norm-clamp effects on generalization timing, but does not measure whether a more efficient circuit replaces memorization, or test the predicted critical dataset size or ungrokking below it.
The paper does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
The paper does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax artifacts.

relationships.condition: Small sparse parity at the study's sizes; LayerNorm variant

source_check.reason: Small sparse parity generalizes immediately without a memorize-first phase, establishing a boundary on the algorithmic setting. Pre-LN reduces the baseline delay to 6,250 versus approximately 20,000 epochs; it changes timing while retaining delayed generalization.

relationships.condition: Plain cross-entropy with clamped total weight norm 35–70 on (a+b) mod 97
relationships.reason: Lower norm gives much faster generalization: 31× slower per +10 norm, fully censored at high norm, hundreds of epochs below the floor (R29, R32).
relationships.display_finding: Each increase of 10 in clamped norm slowed generalization approximately 31-fold; high-norm runs never generalized within observation, while sufficiently low norms yielded generalization within hundreds of epochs.
